question.text: If $k \leq \sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\tan ^{-1} x \leq K,$ then $-$

solution.text:
$\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\tan ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{2}+\tan ^{-1} x$
Since domain of the function $\mathrm{x} \in[-1,1]$ $\therefore-\frac{\pi}{4} \leq \tan ^{-1} x \leq \frac{\pi}{4}$

question.text: If $\cos \cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\cot \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)$, then the value of $x$ is

solution.text:
We have
$\cos \left(\cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)=\cot \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)$
Let $\cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\alpha \Rightarrow \cot \alpha=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \cos ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$
$\Rightarrow \cos \left(\cos ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)=\cot \left(\cot ^{-1} \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{1-x^2}=\sqrt{5} x$
On squaring both sides, we get,
$1-x^2=5 x^2 \Rightarrow 1=6 x^2$
$\Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$
$\begin{array}{ll}& x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \quad \text { [neglecting - ve sign] }\end{array}$

topics.title: Converting one Inverse T function to other Inverse T

solution.text:
Given that,
$\cot \left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)=\sec \left\{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)\right\}$
Since, $\cos ^{-1} x=\cot ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$ and $\tan ^{-1} x=\sec ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \cot \left(\cot ^{-1} \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)=$
$\sec \left\{\sec ^{-1} \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}\right)^2}\right\}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\sqrt{\frac{b^2-a^2+a^2}{b^2-a^2}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\frac{b}{\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}$
On squaring both the sides, we get
$\Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{1-x^2}=\frac{b^2}{b^2-a^2}$
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2-b^2 x^2 \\ & x^2 b^2+b^2 x^2-x^2 a^2=b^2\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 x^2 b^2-x^2 a^2=b^2 \Rightarrow x^2\left(2 b^2-a^2\right)=b^2$
$\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{b}{\sqrt{2 b^2-a^2}}$

question.text: The value of $\cos \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)$ at $x=\frac{1}{5}$ is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \cos \left[2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\pi / 2\right]=-\sin \left[\cos ^{-1} x\right] \\ & =-\sin \left[\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{1-x^2}\right]=-\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ & =-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}=-\sqrt{\frac{24}{25}}=-\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5} \\ & \end{aligned}$

question.text: If $x \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ then the value of $\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{2}(1+\cos 2 x)+\sqrt{\left(\sin ^2 x-48 \cos ^2 x\right) \sin x}\right)$ is equal to

solution.text:
$y=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{2}(1+\cos 2 x)+\sqrt{\left(\sin ^2 x-48 \cos ^2 x\right)} \sin x\right)$
$=\cos ^{-1}\left((7 \cos x)(\cos x)+\sqrt{1-49 \cos ^2 x} \sqrt{1-\cos ^2 x}\right)$
$=\cos ^{-1}(\cos x)-\cos ^{-1}(7 \cos x) \quad[\because \cos x < 7 \cos x]$
$=x-\cos ^{-1}(7 \cos x)$

question.text:
If $\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 a}{1+a^{2}}\right)-\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-b^{2}}{1+b^{2}}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^{2}}\right)$,

then what is the value of $x$ ?

solution.text:
Given,

$\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 a}{1+a^{2}}\right)-\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-b^{2}}{1+b^{2}}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^{2}}\right)$

$\therefore \quad 2 \tan ^{-1} a-2 \tan ^{-1} b=2 \tan ^{-1} x$

$\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1} a-\tan ^{-1} b=\tan ^{-1} x$

$\Rightarrow \quad \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{a-b}{1+a b}\right)=\tan ^{-1} x$

$\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{a-b}{1+a b}$

question.text:
If $\cos ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} \frac{y}{2}=\alpha$,

then $4 x^{2}-4 x y \cos \alpha+y^{2}$ is equal to

solution.text:
$\cos ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} \frac{y}{2}=\alpha$

$\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x y}{2}+\sqrt{\left(1-x^{2}\right)\left(1-\frac{y^{2}}{4}\right)}\right)=\alpha$

$\Rightarrow \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x y+\sqrt{4-y^{2}-4 x^{2}+x^{2} y^{2}}}{2}\right)=\alpha$

$\Rightarrow 4 x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x y \cos \alpha=4 \sin ^{2} \alpha$

question.text: The greatest and least values of $\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}$ are respectively

solution.text:
We have, $\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}+\left(\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}$

$=\left(\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-2 \sin ^{-1} x \cdot \cos ^{-1} x$

$=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}-2 \sin ^{-1} x\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin ^{-1} x\right)$

$=\frac{\pi^{2}}{4}-\pi \sin ^{-1} x+2\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}$

$=2\left[\left(\sin ^{-1} x\right)^{2}-\frac{\pi}{2} \sin ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi^{2}}{8}\right]$

$=2\left[\left(\sin ^{-1} x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right]$

Thus, the least value is $2\left(\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right)$ i.e. $\frac{\pi^{2}}{8}$

and the greatest value is $2\left[\left(\frac{-\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{\pi^{2}}{16}\right]$ i.e. $\frac{5 \pi^{2}}{4} .$

question.text: The value of $\cos \left(2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right)$ at $x=\frac{1}{5}$ is

solution.text:
$\cos \left[2 \cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right]$

$=\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} x+\sin ^{-1} x\right]$

$=\cos \left[\cos ^{-1} x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right]=-\sin \left[\cos ^{-1} x\right]$

$=-\sin \left[\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right]=-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

$=-\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{2}}=-\sqrt{\frac{24}{25}}=-\frac{2 \sqrt{6}}{5}$
